title: Formal Disk4 Solver - End-to-End Pipeline
subtitle: Production search, exact formal resolution, numerical realization, and assembly

pages.title: 1. System overview
pages.subtitle: One candidate moves left to right; side exits classify why it does not continue.

groups.name: CASE MODEL
groups.summary: Choose one catalogue case and materialize its mathematical assumptions.

groups.name: COMBINATORIAL DOMAIN
groups.summary: Enumerate contour assignments and weak cyclic orders.

groups.name: PRE-WORD FORMAL
groups.summary: Compile interface words and apply cheap necessary conditions.

groups.name: WORD RESOLUTION
groups.summary: Explore the canonical Nielsen--Levi residual graph.

groups.name: FORMAL PROFILE
groups.summary: Specialize a family and rebuild exact terminal geometry variables.

groups.name: GEOMETRY + ASSEMBLY
groups.summary: Numerically realize one prototile, then reconstruct all copies.

sidecar.title: MAPPING LAB (EXPERIMENTAL SIDECAR)
sidecar.text: Samples and ranks complete mappings, then evaluates them through a production-filter adapter. Learning changes proposal order only; it does not change production acceptance rules.

pages.title: 2. Catalogue, assignments, and weak-order construction
pages.subtitle: Blue nodes remove equivalent representatives; purple nodes intentionally restrict the question being searched.

cards.title: Select catalogue case
cards.body: Load the case manifest, map builder, search settings, output paths, and checkpoint policy.

cards.title: Validate combinatorial map
cards.body: Check pieces, cyclic contours, vertex incidence, interfaces, hypotheses, and declared automorphisms.

cards.title: Apply imposed search domain
cards.body: Optionally require cyclic equivariance, a cyclic-shift fundamental domain, or a fertile mapping shard. This narrows the question; it is not a quotient proof.

cards.title: Enumerate assignments
cards.body: Choose a cyclic cut/offset and direct or reflected orientation for each copy. The reference orientation fixes the global gauge.

cards.title: Assignment symmetry quotient
cards.body: Keep the lexicographically canonical representative under certified intrinsic map automorphisms compatible with the imposed domain.

cards.title: Start anchored weak order
cards.body: A DFS state is a sequence of coincidence blocks. Block zero contains the reference anchor.

cards.title: Append next-occurrence block
cards.body: Choose a nonempty subset of copies and consume each selected copy's next contour occurrence.

cards.title: Mapping-shard prefix rule
cards.body: When configured, require the next block to remain inside the selected fertile fundamental domain.

cards.title: K4 exterior-arc repetition
cards.body: For the guarded four-tile Stein map, retain a peripheral pair whose two outer-edge endpoints may still coincide.

cards.title: Incremental symmetry canonicality
cards.body: Use the current assignment stabilizer to reject a prefix already larger than an equivalent prefix.

pages.note: The imposed domain and the intrinsic quotient interact, but have different meanings: one changes the requested search space; the other only selects a representative.

pages.title: 3. Weak-order prefix gates and complete Placement emission
pages.subtitle: Only stable information is screened at a prefix; all complete gates are rerun at the leaf.

cards.title: Stable-prefix radius topology
cards.body: Compile only paths that cannot change under descendants, then propagate all known disk-circle arcs.

cards.title: Incremental positive lengths
cards.body: For newly resolved interface rows A x = 0, require a strictly positive normalized length vector.

cards.title: Incremental point angles
cards.body: Add resolved physical vertex sums and require every signed turn to remain in the open interval (-1, 1).

cards.title: Score and generate children
cards.body: Prioritize children that resolve more length and angle equations, then continue depth-first search. This changes order only.

cards.title: Leaf quotient and domain check
cards.body: Canonicalize the complete weak cyclic order and verify the complete imposed-domain predicate.

cards.title: Complete LP witnesses
cards.body: Re-evaluate every resolved length and angle system and request witnesses when available.

cards.title: Complete radius topology
cards.body: Compile every stable interface and outer arc, then run the complete topology necessary condition.

cards.title: Emit Placement
cards.body: Store blocks, positions, exact combinatorial rows, and numerical witness margins for downstream processing.

pages.note: Special cyclic-shift mode constructs one fundamental half/order and its images directly; it still applies every complete leaf gate before emission.

pages.title: 4. Word compilation and radius-arc topology pruning
pages.subtitle: Word equations are exact; green topology exits are intended necessary-condition certificates.

cards.title: Name atomic intervals
cards.body: Turn consecutive weak-order blocks into X0, X1, ... and form the positively oriented prototype contour word.

cards.title: Compile interface equations
cards.body: For each positive-length contact, set the left positive word equal to the inverse right positive word; retain contact parity.

cards.title: Add the mirror sheet
cards.body: Reflected contacts use the explicit mirror involution. Every physical equation also contributes its mirror equation.

cards.title: Compile outer words
cards.body: Record which prototype subwords lie on the positively oriented disk boundary.

cards.title: Seed and transport signed arcs
cards.body: Seed convex radius-R disk arcs. Transport a boundary-aligned contact image with opposite sign; leave a nonaligned image unresolved.

cards.title: Hard outer endpoint gate
cards.body: A transported smooth radius-R arc may not cross a hard outer endpoint, because the endpoint has a forced nonzero turn.

cards.title: Signed-support conflict
cards.body: No positive-length atomic interval may simultaneously carry forced convex and forced concave radius-R support.

cards.title: Forced overlap confirmation
cards.body: When ordering depends on lengths, confirm a forced positive opposite-sign overlap with the exact strict-length system before rejection.

pages.note: The stable-prefix version compiles only descendant-invariant paths. Any unexpected prefix or topology exception conservatively passes rather than rejecting.

pages.title: 5. Exact pre-word metric and turn curriculum
pages.subtitle: The systems are nested in this order; a rejection requires an exact rational contradiction or nonpositive strict margin.

cards.title: Positive atomic lengths
cards.body: Solve homogeneous interface-length equalities with one normalization and require every atomic length to be strictly positive.

cards.title: Local radius measures
cards.body: Introduce signed convex/concave radius-R measures and enforce transport relations induced by boundary-aligned contacts.

cards.title: Local smooth turns
cards.body: Relate smooth-turn variables to signed radius measures and to the oriented interface identifications.

cards.title: Physical point-turn equations
cards.body: Build vertex equivalence classes, sum incident prototype turns at each physical vertex, and enforce -1 < turn < 1.

cards.title: Global radius balance
cards.body: Across n copies require n (L_plus - L_minus) = C_disk, where the signed measures cancel on internal contacts.

cards.title: Global smooth-turn balance
cards.body: Require n * tau_smooth = 2*pi after cancellation of paired internal smooth turns.

cards.title: Strict radius-R concavity
cards.body: When center_strictly_inside_one_tile is declared, require L_minus > 0 on the prototype contour.

cards.title: Isoperimetric bound
cards.body: Apply the necessary perimeter bound C_disk <= sqrt(n) * perimeter(prototype), using a conservative rational upper bound.

pages.note: Floating-point LPs are screens only: an ambiguous or failed numerical solve passes. Rejection is based on the exact rational follow-up.

pages.title: 6. Exact-partial word resolution and family policy
pages.subtitle: Amber exits mean unresolved or unsupported, never a proof of impossibility.

cards.title: Cancel common context
cards.body: Cancel common prefixes and suffixes in every residual word equation.

cards.title: Detect direct contradiction
cards.body: Reject an equation whose reduced sides force an empty word to equal a nonempty constant word.

cards.title: Canonicalize residual state
cards.body: Rename variables canonically, include the mirror environment, and deduplicate already visited residual systems.

cards.title: Generate non-erasing branches
cards.body: Apply the implemented Nielsen prefix substitutions for the leading variables/constants of the chosen residual equation.

cards.title: Update expression environment
cards.body: Compose the substitution into all words and into the symbolic environment, then recurse on the canonical child state.

cards.title: Classify repeated residual
cards.body: Recognize fixed-context residual cycles and compile successive recognized cycles into power or nested-power expressions.

cards.title: Emit canonical family
cards.body: Emit a finite, power, or nested-power environment and validate selected exponent instantiations as a consistency guard.

cards.title: Apply resource guards
cards.body: Bound wall time, graph nodes/edges, residual literals, expression nodes, family count, and terminal contour size.

cards.title: Choose family expansion
cards.body: Specialize finite families. A symbolic power family remains formal unless policy selects concrete exponents.

pages.note: Compile or solver exceptions taint the campaign and may skip the affected work item. They are integrity failures recorded in errors.jsonl, not rejections.

pages.title: 7. Terminal contact system, exact decorations, and profile filters
pages.subtitle: A specialized word family is rebuilt as an exact formal geometry profile before any numerical search.

cards.title: Expand terminal contour
cards.body: Instantiate the selected family environment and materialize the full terminal prototype contour.

cards.title: Verify interface words
cards.body: Recheck every terminal left/right interface identity exactly, including direct/reflected parity and the mirror relation.

cards.title: Build directed segment pairs
cards.body: Create the directed terminal contact records used later by exact decoration and copy assembly.

cards.title: Point-angle classes
cards.body: Identify terminal endpoints that represent the same prototype point-angle variable.

cards.title: Physical vertex sums
cards.body: Assemble exact signed angle equations for every physical vertex of the candidate map.

cards.title: Outer-arc smoothness
cards.body: Impose internal smoothness inside every terminal run labelled as one disk-circle outer arc.

cards.title: Curve-template classes
cards.body: Propagate contact relations and group terminal components that must share a curve template.

cards.title: Normalize terminal lengths
cards.body: Build the exact affine length system, require positive component lengths, and choose a normalized witness.

cards.title: Mark the outer circle
cards.body: Transfer disk-boundary membership and radius-R orientation to terminal contour components.

cards.title: Joint exact feasibility
cards.body: Solve the combined point-angle, curve-turn, length, and winding constraints with a strict feasibility margin.

cards.title: Basic contour invariants
cards.body: Require a nonempty contour, positive exact terminal lengths, and every point angle strictly inside its admissible interval.

cards.title: Angular and winding margin
cards.body: Recheck joint angular feasibility and the exact signed winding/turn margins.

cards.title: Mapping and template coverage
cards.body: Require complete contact coverage, compatible template classes, and a complete outer-circle marking.

cards.title: Conservative dedup + persist
cards.body: Hash map, assignment key, weak-order blocks, and specialization environment; persist one FormalProfile survivor in SQLite/JSONL.

pages.note: Profile-build exceptions taint the campaign. The optional cyclic_no_backtracking heuristic is disabled by default because it has a known counterexample.

pages.title: 8. Numerical prototile geometry and mapping-derived assembly
pages.subtitle: Orange outcomes are numerical evidence only; absence of a solution is not a formal impossibility result.

cards.title: Read FormalProfile survivor
cards.body: Stream candidates.jsonl and skip only profile IDs with a persisted geometric solution.

cards.title: Parse formal geometry problem
cards.body: Load exact affine angle, length, and curve-turn expressions; contact mappings stay attached for later assembly.

cards.title: Parameterize one prototile
cards.body: Generic shared polylines, forced straight segments, and analytic circular arcs; fix origin and initial tangent gauge.

cards.title: Closure least-squares
cards.body: Optimize formal free parameters and generic-template shapes for final point/tangent closure, with bounded random restarts.

cards.title: Full contour validation
cards.body: Check closure, tangent cycle, formal point angles and lengths, positive sampled edges, common radii, area, and sampled self-intersection.

cards.title: Clearance refinement
cards.body: For a closed but colliding/degenerate contour, refine while preserving the closure objective.

cards.title: Persist geometry outcome
cards.body: Valid contour -> geometric_solutions.jsonl. Timeout/exhausted restarts -> no_solution_found status, not a proof.

cards.title: Anchor reference copy
cards.body: Set the reference prototile isometry to identity.

cards.title: Propagate copy isometries
cards.body: Use each directed terminal contact and relative parity to determine neighboring orthogonal transforms.

cards.title: Validate complete contact graph
cards.body: Check connectivity, parity, sampled interface residuals, and consistency across every graph cycle.

cards.title: Index and display
cards.body: Read solution offsets on demand, transform the prototile polygon, and show the assembled pieces in the interactive viewer.

pages.note: The current geometry stage solves a single piece first. It does not optimize all copy placements jointly; assembly is reconstructed deterministically afterward from formal contacts.

pages.title: 9. Meaning of exits and open mathematical provenance
pages.subtitle: Only the first two green/blue classes can support exhaustive formal conclusions.

categories.title: Intrinsic quotient
categories.text: Removes a representative only when a certified automorphism maps it to another enumerated representative.

categories.title: Imposed domain
categories.text: Answers a narrower question by construction (rotation/equivariance/fertile shard); not valid for the unrestricted problem.

categories.title: Necessary-condition rejection
categories.text: Intended mathematical impossibility certificate. Floating screens are conservative; exact rational checks confirm sensitive LP rejections.

categories.title: Deferred / unsupported
categories.text: A graph, expression, family, contour, or time budget ended the attempt. Must never be reported as unsatisfiable.

categories.title: Numerical non-proof
categories.text: Optimization or sampled validation did not find a realization. This is evidence, not a formal rejection.

categories.title: Integrity / implementation error
categories.text: Malformed or inconsistent constructed data, or an unexpected exception. Campaign is tainted when work may have been skipped.

questions.title: Transported exterior-arc repetition theorem
questions.math: For the guarded four-tile Stein map, why must there exist peripheral i != j with the same oriented prototype outer interval, equivalently start_i = start_j and end_i = end_j in the weak cyclic order?
questions.needed: Exact theorem statement, all geometric regularity/center hypotheses, and the Kurusa--Langi--Vigh source or a self-contained proof.

questions.title: Strict radius-R concavity in a Stein configuration
questions.math: Why does center_strictly_inside_one_tile imply L_minus = sum_i r_i^- > 0 on the prototype contour, rather than merely L_minus >= 0?
questions.needed: A proof that a positive-measure disk-circle arc is transported to an internal interface with opposite sign under exactly the hypotheses encoded by the map flag.

questions.title: Completeness of Nielsen branching
questions.math: Why do branch_substitutions enumerate every non-erasing solution of each residual word equation, modulo the canonical renaming/inversion used by the graph?
questions.needed: A standard Nielsen--Levi lemma/citation or a proof tied to the implemented branch cases.

questions.title: Fixed-context residual-cycle compilation
questions.math: Why does a detected cycle V -> p V s generate exactly the family p^n V s^n for all n >= 1, and why do successive compiled cycles preserve completeness for nested powers?
questions.needed: A soundness/completeness proof for classify_fixed_context_loop and the recursion that restarts from the ancestor residual.

pages.warning: The optional cyclic_no_backtracking profile heuristic is disabled by default and has a known counterexample. If enabled, it is explicitly non-mathematical and must not support an exhaustive claim.
